Let \(d=OP\) and \(\beta=\angle OPE\). In right triangle \(OEP\):
\[
\sin\beta=\frac{2}{d},\qquad PE^2=d^2-4.
\]
Since \(OP\) bisects \(\angle EPF\), the angle between \(\overrightarrow{PE}\) and \(\overrightarrow{PF}\) is \(2\beta\). Thus
\[
\overrightarrow{PE}\cdot \overrightarrow{PF}
=(d^2-4)\cos 2\beta
=(d^2-4)\left(1-\frac{8}{d^2}\right)
=d^2-12+\frac{32}{d^2}.
\]
For \(P\in \odot M\), \(OM=5\) and \(PM=1\), so
\[
4\le d\le 6.
\]
Let \(t=d^2\in[16,36]\). Then
\[
f(t)=t-12+\frac{32}{t},\qquad f'(t)=1-\frac{32}{t^2}>0
\]
on \([16,36]\), so the minimum occurs at \(t=16\):
\[
f(16)=16-12+\frac{32}{16}=6.
\]
\[
\boxed{6}
\]
